criteria.name: Identity and source-backed footprint
evidence: Purdue BuildingShapesZip4 snapshot identifies FID 430 as Marc and Sharon Hagle Hall (HAGL).
University project announcement identifies Hagle Hall and states 37,500 square feet and four stories.
The modeled ring is generated from the same 74 GIS vertices; projected ring area recomputes to 845.68 m² (~9103 ft²), 24.3% of stated gross floor area (plausible for four floors).
Footprint evidence is an official campus GIS polygon, not a survey; no building-shape ambiguity is present in the provided crosswalk and article.

criteria.name: Position, orientation, and dimensions
evidence: The asset is a campus-coordinate massing object with identity location/rotation/scale, and its plan bounds closely follow the GIS polygon after the project-mandated approximate WGS84-to-campus conversion.

Position and orientation derive from a single official GIS source. That layer has no populated feature edit date and is explicitly not survey-grade, so independent positional verification remains uncertain.

criteria.name: Height, floors, and roof form
evidence: The official Purdue project announcement supports four stories; the reopened mesh metadata also records 4 stories.
Reopened model height is 15.10 m, but both the source record and model label it estimated; no measured elevation was found.

The revised mesh contains 91 blue canopy-material polygons, extending to Z=15.100000381469727 m. The source photo supports a projecting blue angular roof/canopy above the curved bay, while exact canopy geometry and elevations remain visual estimates.
A broad flat top plate is still present; the source photo is oblique and does not provide a roof plan or measured elevations.

criteria.name: Facade, entrances, and distinctive architecture
evidence: The Purdue construction photo supports dark brick wings, a pale curved glazed bay, and a glazed ground level; corresponding colors, corner treatment, and broad window bands are present in the preview.

Freshly reopened mesh contains 51 glazing faces along the NW curved-bay coordinate region; this verifies that the revision added a broadly glazed faceted curve. The source image shows glazing across the curve but also stone/opaque divisions that remain simplified.

The mesh includes 1 inset low-level entry glazing face(s) and 5 nearby metal-frame face(s), verifying that a framed door is present. In the single saved perspective it is still small and difficult to distinguish from adjacent storefront glazing; exact placement is not dimensioned.

criteria.name: Modular export, portability, and evidence
evidence: Independent Blender 5.2 background reopen found scene Building_massing_marc_and_sharon_hagle_hall_hagl_071ffd6, expected collection Asset_massing_marc_and_sharon_hagle_hall_hagl_071ffd6, one mesh object, 4716 vertices, and 1144 faces.
Object transform is location=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], rotation=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], scale=[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]; there are 0 modifiers, 0 linked libraries, and 0 file-backed images.

Manifest names the same asset, scene, collection, and object (['Marc and Sharon Hagle Hall (HAGL)']); structured evidence includes raw GIS, official project announcements, project photos, source URLs, dates, CRS/method notes, and a preview.

findings.finding: The rebuilt blue canopy projects above/out from the curved bay and is visible in the preview, addressing the prior missing-feature finding. It reads as a multi-faceted curved ribbon rather than the sharper angular canopy in the source photo, and exact canopy dimensions are unsupported.

The NW curve now has continuous glazing, the projecting blue canopy is present, and the reopened mesh contains an inset framed door. The source photo shows opaque stone bands/divisions within the curved volume; the entrance is still difficult to pick out in the saved camera view, and the canopy reads as a curved ribbon rather than the sharper angular form in the photo.
The 15.1 m height is an estimate from four stories and assumed floor heights/parapet; the sources do not establish measured eave, roof, or parapet heights.

The GIS polygon supplies footprint and orientation evidence but no survey accuracy or populated feature edit date; campus placement is supported by that geometry and the official address/location description, not an independent survey.
